Robot Doctor Autonomous

Autonomous is different every run

Works once, then misses. Ends in a different spot each time. Below are the 7 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does your autonomous move by time (power + sleep) instead of distance? For example: setPower(0.5); sleep(1200);
  • Do you line the robot up exactly the same way every time? Same wall, same tile seam, same angle, ideally with a jig or a mark.
  • Do you track position with dead wheels or a Pinpoint / OTOS (not just drive motor encoders)? Dead wheels are small unpowered omni wheels with encoders.
  • Does it jump straight to full power at the start of moves? No ramp-up or motion profile.
  • Does it still happen with a freshly charged battery? Swap to a battery straight off the charger and repeat the exact same thing.
  • Are you using a path follower (Pedro Pathing, Road Runner)? A library that follows paths using odometry.
  • Does the localization test pass (push 48" forward → X ≈ 48, left → Y up, heading correct)? Run your library's localization test OpMode and push the robot by hand.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Autonomous drives by time

sleep()-timed driving goes a different distance every time because battery voltage and traction change.

How to fix it 1 hr

  1. Replace "drive for 1.2 seconds" with "drive until the encoder or odometry says 24 inches".
  2. Correct heading with the IMU while driving straight.
  3. Best: use odometry with a path follower like Pedro Pathing or Road Runner.

Sources: GM0 · Encoders · GM0 · Dead wheels

2 Robot starts in a slightly different spot

An inch or a few degrees off at the start becomes much more by the end of the path.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Line the robot up against the wall and a tile seam the same way every time. Mark it in your notebook.
  2. Build a simple alignment jig or use the robot's flat sides against field features.

Sources: GM0 · Dead wheels

3 Wheels slip under hard acceleration

Slamming to full power makes mecanum wheels slip, so the robot ends somewhere different each run.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Ramp power up and down instead of jumping to full, or use a motion profile.
  2. Lower the max acceleration in your path follower.

Sources: GM0 · Control loops

4 Battery is low or worn out

A tired battery sags under load, so motors slow down and the hub can brown out.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Swap in a freshly charged battery and test again. That alone answers the question.
  2. Watch the voltage on the Driver Station while you drive hard. Healthy packs dip, but sitting around 9 V or lower under load is a problem.
  3. Charge at the rate the battery maker recommends (REV slim: 1.8 A on the REV charger; TETRIX: 0.9 A).
  4. Label every battery with your team number, the year, and a name, and tally charge cycles. NiMH packs get weak after roughly 200–300 cycles.
  5. Retire packs that drop fast even when full. A battery tester (like a Battery Beak) shows internal resistance.

Sources: FTC Docs · Battery care, charging, fuses · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · REV · 12V battery troubleshooting

5 Tracking with drive-motor encoders

Mecanum wheels slip, especially when accelerating hard, so drive encoders lose track over a match.

How to fix it varies

  1. Limit acceleration in autonomous so wheels do not slip.
  2. For accurate autos, add dead wheels or a Pinpoint / OTOS, and correct with AprilTags when you can see them.

Sources: GM0 · Dead wheels

6 Localization isn't accurate yet

A path follower can only be as good as its position estimate. Bad localization looks exactly like bad tuning.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. Tune localization before any follower or PID tuning.
  2. Run the localization test: push forward 48" and check X ≈ 48, push left and check Y goes up, spin and check heading.
  3. Only move on once every check passes.

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

7 Dead wheel loses contact with the floor

Without enough spring force, a pod skips or lifts over seams and stops counting accurately.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Push down on each pod. It should spring back firmly and always touch the tiles.
  2. Add spring or rubber band tension so the wheel stays planted, and make sure it moves freely up and down.
  3. Check the pod wheel spins freely and the encoder cable has slack for the pod to move.

Sources: GM0 · Dead wheels
